steps.title: Welcome to the Lab
steps.instruction:
Welcome to the Token Optimization - The Credit Crunch lab.

You will run a controlled before-and-after experiment for a dependency upgrade planning workflow. First, save the workflow and measure a successful baseline. Then add one justified customization, repeat the same request, and compare the supported cost and debug surfaces.

You will also evaluate whether a skill or custom agent solves a distinct remaining need. The goal is not to build every artifact. It is to find the smallest setup that improves cost per successful outcome.

steps.title: Create the Results Worksheet
steps.instruction: We've opened a new file. Save it as token-optimization-results.md in the workspace so your baseline and optimized results survive the lab.

steps.title: Save the Experiment Plan
steps.instruction:
Add this worksheet structure, then save the file:

# Dependency Upgrade Experiment
## Workflow
Inputs: package manifest, lockfile, and documented test command
Steps: inspect dependencies, select one upgrade candidate, identify likely breaking changes, and produce a plan
Guardrails: do not edit files; inspect only dependency and directly relevant configuration files
Definition of done: name one candidate and provide a concise, evidence-based upgrade plan

## Baseline
Credits:
Session tokens:
Accepted outcome: yes/no
Notes:

## Optimized
Credits:
Session tokens:
Accepted outcome: yes/no
Notes:
steps.tip: The accepted outcome matters. A cheaper run that fails the definition of done is not an optimization.

steps.title: Open Copilot Chat
steps.instruction: We've opened Copilot Chat. Select Agent mode and keep the default model strategy for both runs.

steps.title: Run and Record the Baseline
steps.instruction:
Send this exact request:

Inspect this workspace's package manifest, lockfile, and directly relevant configuration. Select one dependency upgrade candidate and produce a concise upgrade plan with likely breaking changes. Do not edit files.

When the response finishes, verify it meets the definition of done. Hover over the response to record its AI Credits. Open the context-window control to record cumulative session tokens. Add both values and your acceptance decision under Baseline, then save the worksheet.
steps.tip: If the workspace has no package manifest, use a repository that does and keep that same repository for the optimized run.

validate.label: Baseline section records cost and outcome fields

steps.title: Panels Closed
steps.instruction:
We've closed the editor tab and Copilot Chat for you.

For future reference:
• New File: Ctrl+N
• Copilot Chat: Ctrl+Alt+I

steps.title: Create a Scoped Instruction
steps.instruction: We've opened a new file. Save it as .github/instructions/dependency-migration.instructions.md. Create the .github/instructions folders first if this workspace does not have them.

steps.title: Write Only Standing Rules
steps.instruction:
Add this content, then save the file:

---
applyTo: "**/{package.json,package-lock.json,pnpm-lock.yaml,yarn.lock}"
---

- Use the repository's existing package manager.
- During planning, inspect only the manifest, lockfile, and directly relevant configuration.
- Do not edit files.
- Name one candidate and report evidence, likely breaking changes, and the validation command.

This is the experiment's only customization. It adds context, so it must improve the outcome or reduce downstream work to earn its place.
steps.tip: Keep detailed upgrade procedures out of standing instructions. They can be evaluated separately as an on-demand skill.

validate.label: Instruction is scoped and preserves the planning guardrail

steps.title: Open a Fresh Chat
steps.instruction: We've opened Copilot Chat. Start a New Chat, select Agent mode, and keep the same model strategy as the baseline. A fresh session prevents baseline history from affecting the comparison.

steps.title: Run the Optimized Workflow
steps.instruction:
Send the identical baseline request:

Inspect this workspace's package manifest, lockfile, and directly relevant configuration. Select one dependency upgrade candidate and produce a concise upgrade plan with likely breaking changes. Do not edit files.

Verify the same definition of done. Hover over the response for AI Credits, then open the context-window control for session tokens. Open token-optimization-results.md, record the values and acceptance decision under Optimized, and save it.

Compare only successful outcomes. Keep the instruction only if it improves cost, quality, consistency, or avoided rework enough to justify its recurring context.
steps.tip: A small increase in one-turn tokens can still be worthwhile if the instruction prevents retries or corrections. Record that evidence in Notes.

validate.label: Optimized cost and outcome are recorded

steps.title: Panels Closed
steps.instruction:
We've closed the editor tab and Copilot Chat for you.

For future reference:
• New File: Ctrl+N
• Copilot Chat: Ctrl+Alt+I

steps.title: Open Copilot Chat
steps.instruction: We've opened Copilot Chat so you can evaluate whether this workflow has a detailed procedure worth loading on demand.

steps.title: Evaluate an On-Demand Skill
steps.instruction:
A skill is justified if this team repeatedly performs the full upgrade procedure, not just planning. If that need exists, select Agent mode and run:

/create-skill A dependency upgrade procedure that reads release notes, applies documented migration steps only to affected modules, runs the repository's validation commands, and summarizes the evidence.

If the need does not exist, skip creation and record Skill not justified in the worksheet Notes. Skipping an unnecessary artifact is a valid optimization result.
steps.tip: If you create the skill, rerun the controlled experiment later as a separate change. Do not combine it with the instruction result.

steps.title: Panels Closed
steps.instruction:
We've closed the sidebar for you.

For future reference:
• Copilot Chat: Ctrl+Alt+I

steps.title: Open Copilot Chat
steps.instruction: We've opened Copilot Chat so you can evaluate whether the workflow needs a durable role or constrained tool set.

steps.title: Evaluate a Custom Agent
steps.instruction:
A custom agent is justified if this workflow needs a reusable role, model choice, or constrained tool set. If that need exists, first select Agent mode, then run:

/create-agent A migration assistant that upgrades dependencies, edits only affected modules, and runs repository validation. Limit tools to repository search, file edits, and terminal commands.

If the instruction or skill already supplies enough control, skip creation and record Custom agent not justified in the worksheet Notes.
steps.tip: A smaller tool list can reduce discovery overhead, but it must still contain every tool required for the accepted outcome.

steps.title: Panels Closed
steps.instruction:
We've closed the sidebar for you.

For future reference:
• Copilot Chat: Ctrl+Alt+I

steps.title: Open Agent Debug Logs
steps.instruction: We've opened the Command Palette. Run Developer: Open Agent Debug Logs to inspect the session you measured. If logs are unavailable, enable github.copilot.chat.agentDebugLog.fileLogging.enabled in Settings, run one fresh measured request, and reopen the panel.

steps.title: Inspect the Expensive Path
steps.instruction:
Use the supported views to explain the result:
• Summary: compare session tokens, tool calls, errors, and duration
• Logs: locate unnecessary exploration, retries, or repeated tool calls
• Chat Debug: confirm which instructions, context, and tool definitions were sent
• Cache Explorer: compare consecutive model turns and locate the first prefix divergence

Add one evidence-based explanation to the worksheet Notes. Do not copy prompt or response content into shared records unless your organization's policy allows it.
steps.tip: If the command is unavailable, update VS Code and GitHub Copilot, then use the response hover and context-window measurements you already recorded.

steps.title: Panels Closed
steps.instruction:
We've closed the Agent Debug Logs editor for you.

For future reference:
• Command Palette: Ctrl+Shift+P

steps.title: Lab Complete!
steps.instruction:
Congratulations! You have completed the Token Optimization lab.

You practiced an evidence-based optimization loop:
• Saved a dependency-upgrade workflow with guardrails and an accepted outcome
• Measured a successful baseline with per-response credits and session tokens
• Added one scoped instruction and repeated the identical request in a fresh session
• Compared cost and outcome before deciding whether to keep the artifact
• Evaluated skills and custom agents only for distinct remaining needs
• Used Agent Debug Logs and Cache Explorer to explain the measured result

The target is the smallest repeatable cost for an accepted outcome, not the fewest tokens in isolation.
